title: Kids in the Kitchen, by Age
summary: What children can do in the kitchen at ages 3 to 5, 6 to 8, 9 to 12 and 13 and up, with a grown-up: jobs, words and tools to learn, first recipes, measuring practice from the Math Ladder, knife skills, and table setting from the Etiquette Ladder.

list: A grown-up is in the kitchen whenever a child cooks.
Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds before you start, and after touching raw meat, poultry or eggs.
Turn pot and pan handles in, away from the edge of the stove.
Use oven mitts for anything that has been on the stove or in the oven.
Never leave the stove on and walk away.
Unplug appliances before cleaning them or reaching near blades.
Don’t taste raw dough or batter, or food that isn’t cooked yet.
Clean up together. Cleaning is part of cooking.
p: Every child is different. The ages below are a guide; move on when a child shows they’re ready.
Learn these two holds on soft foods first, with a grown-up showing how.

cards.p: Curl the fingertips of the hand holding the food under, like a bear’s claw, with the thumb tucked behind. The knuckles guide the side of the blade, and the fingertips stay out of the way.

For round foods like a potato or tomato: make a bridge over the food with the thumb on one side and fingers on the other. Cut down through the gap under the bridge. Then lay the flat side down so it can’t roll.

list: Put a damp towel under the board so it doesn’t slide.
Carry a knife with your arm at your side and the point down.
Never put a knife into a sink full of water; wash it and put it away.

age.intro: Little hands love to stir, pour and wash. Stay right beside them every minute.
tasks: Wash hands with soap for 20 seconds, the first job every time
Rinse fruit and vegetables in a bowl of water
Stir and mix batters
Pour from a small pitcher
Brush oil onto bread or vegetables with a pastry brush
Cut cookie and sandwich shapes with cutters
Mash bananas or cooked potatoes
Tear lettuce
Wipe the table and carry unbreakable things
age.knife: No sharp knives. With a grown-up, a plastic or butter knife can cut soft foods like banana on a board.
age.measure: Fill and pour: which cup holds more? Count scoops of oats into a bowl.
age.setting: Put a napkin, a fork and a cup at each place.

age.intro: Ready for real steps of a recipe. A grown-up is still in the kitchen, and abilities vary a lot, so match the job to the child.
tasks: Crack eggs into a bowl, then wash hands
Measure dry ingredients and level them off
Peel carrots and potatoes with a vegetable peeler, peeling away from the hand
Snip herbs and green onions with blunt kitchen shears
Shuck corn and prepare lettuce for a salad
Beat eggs with a whisk
Load the dishwasher (knives go in with a grown-up, or get hand-washed)
Scoop out avocado halves after a grown-up cuts them
age.knife: Practice the claw and bridge holds on soft foods (cucumber, banana, cooked potato) with a butter knife or a kid-safe knife, a grown-up right beside them.

math.t: Grade 3: Fractions on the Number Line

age.measure: How many ¼ cups fill 1 cup? How many teaspoons make a tablespoon? Weigh an apple on the scale.
age.setting: Set a simple place: plate in the middle, fork on the left, knife and spoon on the right, cup above the knife.

age.intro: Can follow a whole recipe with a grown-up nearby. Before working more on their own, check that they know the stove, oven and knife rules below.
tasks: Read a recipe all the way through, then gather everything first
Measure accurately, liquid and dry
Open cans with a can opener
Use a food thermometer to check that food is done
Boil pasta and simmer sauces on the stove
Bake in the oven with oven mitts
Use the microwave safely
Slice and chop vegetables
Put leftovers in shallow containers and refrigerate them within 2 hours
Plan a simple family meal
age.knife: Slicing and chopping vegetables with a sharp knife, using the claw and bridge, on a board that doesn’t slide. A grown-up supervises.

math.t: Grade 4: Converting Larger Units to Smaller
Grade 5: Converting Units in Multistep Problems

age.measure: Double a recipe or cut it in half. The meal planner scales recipes too: check its math.
age.setting: Set the whole family table, with glasses, napkins and serving spoons.

age.intro: Can cook whole meals and learn why recipes work. Still check in on knife, stove and food safety habits.
tasks: Cook a full dinner from start to finish
Change a recipe once they know how it works
Brown meat and check it with a thermometer
Roast a chicken or a sheet-pan dinner
Plan meals and a shopping list on a budget
Clean as they go and sanitize after raw meat
Care for cast iron and knives
words: mise en place (French: “everything in its place”)
age.knife: Full chef’s knife skills: the claw grip, rocking cuts, dicing an onion, honing before use, hand-washing and safe storage.
age.measure: Convert a recipe from cups to grams with the kitchen scale. Work out the cost per serving.
age.setting: Set a formal table and host a family dinner.

links.d: A matching game with the kitchen tool drawings.
Print the jobs for each age and hang it on the fridge.
Learn 3 teaspoons to a tablespoon, 2 cups to a pint and the rest by heart.
